gap: No result ChatGPT got says how many watt-hours a 1 kWh station takes in to go from empty to full. StorageReview measured 1,180 Wh into the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus and 1,360 Wh into the BLUETTI AC180, and Notebookcheck measured 1,110 Wh into the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2. Divided by each solar limit, that gives a refill floor of about 1.2 h, 1.85 h and 2.7 h.
standout_why: I opened amphourly.com (DELTA 3 Plus vs Explorer 1000 v2), powerstations.reviews (Explorer 1000 v2 solar setups) and testedwatts.com (Jackery vs Anker). All three work out refill time from rated or assumed capacity and give no measured energy-in. Amphourly even divides an assumed 870 Wh of usable capacity by 1,000 W and gets 1.0 h, which is shorter than the measured energy-in allows. ChatGPT's cited sources are EcoFlow's '70 minutes' and Anker's '1.8 hours', both maker claims. solargenreview.com returned HTTP 429 and verifiedbackuppowerdata.com failed its TLS check, so I could not check those two. No one in the result set has a named, measured refill figure.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. On measured energy-in, the DELTA 3 Plus needs about 1,180 Wh ÷ 1,000 W ≈ 1.2 h (about 71 min), which supports EcoFlow's 70-minute claim. The C1000 Gen 2 needs 1,110 Wh ÷ 600 W ≈ 1.85 h and the AC180 needs 1,360 Wh ÷ 500 W ≈ 2.7 h. The order is the same as ChatGPT's, but the page can now say 'measured' and give honest floors. No named reviewer measured a full two-panel solar refill on any candidate. The only two-input observation is The Solar Lab getting 'really close to 1,000W combined' on the DELTA 3 Plus.

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus Review - StorageReview (Dylan Dougherty, 2025-01-02)
findings.note: StorageReview: 'The unit required 1.18kWh (1,180Wh) to recharge fully.' The test was an AC charge. Solar goes through the DC MPPT input, so losses may differ. Floor at the 1,000 W solar limit: 1,180 ÷ 1,000 = 1.18 h ≈ 71 min, consistent with EcoFlow's 70-minute claim.

unsourced: A named reviewer's measured two-panel solar refill time, with logged watts and hours, for any candidate. I checked StorageReview, Notebookcheck, OutdoorGearLab, CleanTechnica, PopSci, The Drive and The Solar Lab. The Solar Lab's C1000 Gen 2 '1.5 to 2 hours' with solar gives no panels, watts or conditions, so I left it out.
Measured energy-in to refill the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2. OutdoorGearLab gives only charge rates and times.
Energy-in measured through the solar (DC) input rather than AC for any candidate. All the energy-in figures above are AC wall charges.
The contents of solargenreview.com (HTTP 429) and verifiedbackuppowerdata.com (TLS certificate error). I could not open either to compare.
